title: Windows 10
wiki_lead:
Windows 10 is a major release of the Windows NT operating system developed by Microsoft. The successor to Windows 8.1, it was released to manufacturing on July 15, 2015, became generally available on July 29, 2015, and was a free upgrade to users of Windows 7, 8, and 8.1. Its server counterparts are Windows Server 2016, 2019, and 2022. It was succeeded by Windows 11 in October 2021. 
In contrast to the tablet-oriented approach of its predecessor, Windows 10 returned to a desktop-oriented interface in line with previous versions of Windows and reintroduced the Start menu. Other features included the Cortana virtual assistant, Task View and virtual desktops, Action Center, biometric authentication through Windows Hello, an improved Settings component, Xbox Live integration, and DirectX 12. Also, Microsoft Edge was introduced, deprecating Internet Explorer. Unlike previous NT releases, Windows 10 received free feature updates on an ongoing basis. Alternatively, enterprise environments can use long-term support milestones that receive only critical and security updates. An ARM version of Windows 10 was released in 2018.
Windows 10 received generally positive reviews. Praise was given to the return of the desktop interface, improved bundled software compared to Windows 8.1, and other capabilities, while criticism was directed at behavioral changes such as mandatory update installation, privacy concerns over data collection, and adware-like tactics to promote the operating system on release. Microsoft aimed to have Windows 10 installed on over a billion devices within three years of release; ultimately, that goal was reached in March 2020, almost five years later. By January 2018, it surpassed Windows 7 as the most popular version of Windows worldwide, until Windows 11 took the top spot in June 2025. As of October 2026, Windows 10 is the second-most-used version of Windows, accounting for 25% worldwide share, while Windows 11 holds 74%.
It is the last version of Windows that supports 32-bit processors, BIOS firmware, and systems with no TPM or TPM 1.2; it is also the last to officially lack a CPU model check before installation. Support ended on October 14, 2025, except for editions in the Long-Term Servicing Channel (LTSC) or enrolled in the Extended Security Updates program.

Development
At the Microsoft Worldwide Partner Conference in 2011, Andrew Lees, the chief of Microsoft's mobile technologies, said that the company intended to have a single software ecosystem for PCs, smartphones, tablets, and other devices: "We won't have an ecosystem for PCs, and one for phones, and one for tablets‍—‌they'll all come together."
In December 2013, technology writer Mary Jo Foley reported that Microsoft was working on an update to Windows 8 codenamed "Threshold", after a planet in its Halo franchise. grok_lead: Windows 10 is a major release of the Microsoft Windows operating system, part of the Windows NT operating system line, designed to deliver a unified, mobile-first experience across personal computers, tablets, embedded systems, and other devices. It was publicly released on July 29, 2015, following a technical preview period that began in 2014, and marked Microsoft's shift toward a "Windows as a service" model with ongoing feature updates. Support for most editions of Windows 10 concluded on October 14, 2025, after which Microsoft ceased providing free security updates and technical support, though extended security updates are available for purchase. Windows 10 emphasized natural user interactions and cross-device continuity, introducing features such as the Cortana virtual assistant for voice-activated search and productivity tasks, the Microsoft Edge web browser (formerly Project Spartan) for faster rendering and annotation capabilities, and Continuum mode to seamlessly adapt the interface between desktop and tablet layouts on hybrid devices. It also restored the traditional Start menu while integrating live tiles from Windows 8, added support for virtual desktops via Task View, and enhanced gaming with Xbox Live integration and DirectX 12 for improved graphics performance. These innovations aimed to bridge the gap between traditional PC computing and emerging form factors like holographic displays via compatibility with devices such as Microsoft HoloLens. The operating system was offered as a free upgrade for the first year to users of genuine copies of Windows 7 and 8.1, contributing to rapid adoption with more than 75 million devices running Windows 10 within the first month of release. Windows 10 supported a wide array of editions, including Home, Pro, Enterprise, and Education, with semi-annual feature updates like the Anniversary Update (version 1607) and the final version 22H2 released in October 2022. By prioritizing privacy controls, biometric authentication through Windows Hello, and universal apps that run across platforms, Windows 10 solidified Microsoft's focus on secure, versatile computing until the transition to Windows 11. Even after the end of support on October 14, 2025, official installation media downloads for Windows 10 remain available from Microsoft at https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/software-download/windows10, where users can download ISO files directly or use the Media Creation Tool, with 32-bit (x86) and 64-bit options offered based on the CPU and system type. Microsoft recommends upgrading to Windows 11 for continued security updates, new features, and technical support.
